items.title: HIS BLOCK, AS A PLACE YOU ARRIVE AT
items.why: The three settlement screens are sizes, not places: camp, town and fortress are how big a town is, and none of them is anywhere. This is the fourth one and it is your own block, with your door and your step, your drive with the wreck still on it, next door's gate shut and his table out, and the board at the kerb, and you see it in the VOTE tab by day and at night.

diffs: COLOURS PER TEN THOUSAND PIXELS: his 6090.1, ours 113.8. Ours is built from six-step ramps, so it bands where his reads as a surface.
COLOURS TO COVER HALF THE PICTURE: his 964, ours 4. He bought a surface; we drew a palette.

items.title: THE BAR, AND WHAT WE MADE
items.why: You said the art looks nothing like the assets we downloaded, and you were right: all 1,927 tiles you bought and approved back in July were sitting in a bank file as code, so nobody was looking at them, and they are real files now, sorted into seven families with a sheet of each. You see it in the VOTE tab, your own street tiles on top and ours underneath at the same size, with the three measured differences under them.

items.title: THE FAR END'S GROUND, CUT FROM HIS OWN TILES
items.why: The map's ground was a flat tan square of fifty near-identical tans, which is why the far end read like paper, so every land cell is now cut from the terrain tiles you picked and approved back in July. You see it in the VOTE tab, the same patch of valley before and after at the same size.

before_after.before: the far end's ground painted by this lane, 24 by 8 cells of the valley
before_after.after: the same 24 by 8 cells cut from the terrain tiles he picked and approved

WHAT IS STILL OURS: road, spine and water, because his terrain picks hold none of those, and the yard's painted marks were lost in the re-cut.

items.title: THE MAP'S MARKERS, SO YOU CAN FIND THEM
items.why: The place markers on the map were dark shapes on a dark map, so on rock or at the map's edge you could not see them at all and another chat had to draw an outline round them to make them usable. They are lit now with the colours off your own approved tiles, and you see it in the VOTE tab, the same five markers on the same five grounds, before and after.

before_after.before: the five markers as they are on the map today, on all five grounds, with no outline
before_after.after: the same five, same shapes, lit from his own approved tiles, same grounds, no outline

WHERE THE COLOUR CAME FROM: his own approved tiles for the thing each marker is (his market stalls, roofs, pipes and walls), hue measured off them, never picked.
WHAT DID NOT CHANGE: not one pixel of silhouette, and every moving part still moves (the banner stirs, the shed's sheet lifts, the pump's beam nods).

items.title: CLIMBING: A MAN'S CARD BEFORE AND AFTER A FIGHT
items.why: After a won fight each man gets his XP, at 200 he hits level 2, three stats go up in green by his stars, and he picks one of nine first-tier perks that he carries into the next fight. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, before on the left and after on the right.

items.title: THE CELLS THAT ALL OPEN THE SAME FIGHT
items.why: The whole valley coloured by which fight board each cell loads, and the lit ones all load the SAME board: the airfield, the speedway, the stadium, every civic building, and three of the six big gear places. Twenty four of our seventy eight kinds of place fall through to one fallback, which is more than any real board gets, and you see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, NOT IN A TAB YET on a play surface.

items.title: THE FREEWAY'S FIVE WRONG PIECES, FIXED
items.why: The barrier is now cast concrete, the lines are the street's white and a faded yellow instead of orange, the trailer is a real rusted box, the asphalt is patched and cracked, and the dark band is gone. Thumbs up and the freeway looks like this in every fight, and you see it in the COMBAT tab on the freeway board.

items.title: THE TITLE SHOWS UP IN 2.7 SECONDS ON A PHONE, WAS 3.5
items.why: The old fight that the demo never opens was still half of the page a phone downloads, so the demo is now cut without it and the title comes up in 2.7 seconds instead of 3.5 on a phone-speed processor (the goal is 2). You see it on the demo's start screen: the title and its buttons show up sooner after you tap the link.

items.title: HAIRSTYLES THAT MATCH
items.why: The hair picker showed the right 11 names but lost two of its six dials every time you clicked one, so three cuts drew the same cap and one lost its texture; both are wired now, worst pair down from 93% identical to 89%. You see it in the VOTE tab.

items.title: THE WHOLE CROWD MATCHES
items.why: Every citizen in the valley got a random hair texture on their portrait instead of their real one; 76 of 82 textured citizens disagreed with their own body. Fixed and shipped, not a vote -- you see it in the VOTE tab as proof.

items.title: THE ENEMY FACES
items.why: Every brigand tier's portrait had none of its own dressed body's haircut, not even by accident; now all six wear the real cut, and the leader's face gets a second light so he reads as the one you remember. You see it in the VOTE tab.

items.title: THE KEEPERS SPEAK
items.why: The smith now has a real price line to say, with a real trait line and a real rumour already waiting on the same mouth. You see it in the VOTE tab, item THE KEEPERS SPEAK.

items.title: BY GENERATION THREE THE VALLEY SHOULD REMEMBER ONE STORY, A LITTLE WRONG.
items.why: Right now a deed fades but is never forgotten, while real people remember the name, one merged story and the grudges still alive. You see it in the VOTE tab, on this card.

show.src: Measured: seven retold deeds went through two generations and all seven were still there, just fainter.\nReal memory: the name lasts, the details drift, one story absorbs the rest.\nProposal: generation three keeps the name, ONE legend line (a little wrong), living grudges, and a place name. The rest is gone.

items.title: THE PHONE SHOWS THE JOBS
items.why: The phone now shows the two nearest places that are hiring and what they pay, with skulls for the danger; it shows them but never takes them, you take a job at the place, and a job you took disappears from the phone. You see it on the map, at the top of the phone.

items.title: AN ID IS A PROMISE
items.why: A mod finds every row by its id, so renaming one of the 725 ids breaks the 764 places that point at them. You see it in the VOTE tab, with the four rules that keep mods working.

items.title: EVERY ROLL A MAN MAKES
items.why: The wiki's stars, level and XP numbers on one page, with a red box where the demo differs: 1 to 3 starred stats instead of exactly 3, random level-up stats, and wages that never rise. You see it in the VOTE tab, on its own page.

items.title: VIA GROK: A MISSED PAYDAY MAKES A HIRE LEAVE A COUPLE OF DAYS AFTER THE BATTERIES HIT ZERO, NEVER THE SAME DAY
items.why: Grok reports you said a hire who is not paid walks only a couple of days after your batteries hit zero, not the same day, and his traits stretch or shrink that clock (a greedy man sooner). You see it on the roster screen as a man's mood dropping after the missed noon and his leaving on the second or third morning.

show.src:
VIA GROK, pages GROK_141 and GROK_143 (the wiki's Mood page: not paid is -1 mood, greedy -2, not eaten -1; angry 0 to 15 percent may desert; mood drifts back when nothing happens). The wiki gives no day count; his 'a couple of days' is the number.

Seen in: the roster screen's mood line; the morning a man is gone.

items.title: A TOWN BEFORE AND AFTER A RAID
items.why: A crew that reaches a town unopposed leaves it raided (half the items, half the recruits), and a caravan leaves it well supplied, using Battle Brothers' own two pages. You see it in the VOTE tab: two towns on one real valley, before and after.

items.title: EVERY SETTLEMENT HAS ITS OWN SHELF, NEVER ITS OWN PRICE
items.why: Battle Brothers moves a town's price with raids and supply; ours keeps the one-battery price locked and moves the SHELF instead, cut thin after a raid and fuller on market day. You see it in the records, not drawn yet, feeding TUNING and the settlement screen.

show.src:
records/BOHEMIA_ECONOMY_DAY_62_EVERY_SETTLEMENT_HAS_ITS_OWN_SHELF_NEVER_ITS_OWN_PRICE_10_9_26.md; banks/BOHEMIA_ECONOMY_TEST_LINES_9_5_26.md round 62.

Seen in: not drawn yet, feeds TUNING and the settlement screen.

items.title: THE PEOPLE OF THE PLACE: KEEPERS AT THEIR DOORS, A CROWD BY THE STALL
items.why: COOK's finished pictures are in, and now a keeper breathes, smokes or haggles at every door while a crowd by the stall swells to eleven on market day and drops to one when the town is raided or sick. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, and in the demo when you arrive at any town.

items.title: THE FOUR PHONES: CRACKED, REPAIRED, THE SLAB, YELLOWED
items.why: Your phone at each act, rendered live on the game's own phone: cracked in act 1, taped in a rubber bumper in act 2, a clean metal slab if act 3 went well, yellowed and shattered if it went badly. You see it on the map's phone, four versions side by side.

items.title: DO THE THIRTEEN STILL READ APART, SMALL
items.why: Battle Brothers reads a man's kit by shape, not colour, because its camera is often far, so I shrank all thirteen gang looks down to a small figure and measured whether each one is still its own shape or colour. Thumbs up, and you see it here, with two pairs honestly flagged as the closest calls for DIRECTION and COOK to look at.

items.title: THE THREE BLOCKS THE VALLEY NEEDS
items.why: Four fight boards: the stadium bowl, the water plant, the hospital, and a casino floor with two hundred slot machines on it. The first three are cut from the real city, the hospital is a solid slab because nothing in this whole valley has an inside you can walk into, and the casino is the one room anybody ever built and no part of the game can currently reach it, and you see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, NOT IN A TAB YET on a play surface.

items.title: A NEW PHONE OPENS ON THE START SCREEN, NOT IN THE CITY
items.why: A test walk skipped the start screen by clicking the hidden BEGIN behind it, so the game looked like it dropped strangers mid-game; now nothing but NEW GAME or CONTINUE gets you in, and the screen stays dark until the start screen is drawn. You see it when the DEMO first opens: before on the left, the start screen and the crew picks on the right.

items.title: WHO DIES AT ZERO, AND WHAT THE OTHERS CARRY HOME
items.why: A man struck down dies one time in five, else he lives with one of Battle Brothers' permanent injuries (a missing eye, a broken knee) and is laid up 30 to 40 days, you never die, and the recap and the roster say who and with what; by day every man now wears a dark one-pixel edge so he reads in the sun. Lose a man in a fight and you see it on the recap, in the VOTE tab and the demo, NOT IN A TAB YET.

items.title: FOUR LEGS
items.why: The first lab-made beast moves: a dire wolf walks in, breaks into a lope with a moment in the air, bites the man with its jaws open, takes his swing and goes down, three pictures a beat like the men. Before, the fight had nothing on four legs to draw, and you see it before beside now, plus the same two at the map's size, in the VOTE tab (in the fight itself once COMBAT reads the beast sheet, NOT IN A TAB YET).
items.said: just beasts human genetically brought back but broke out their labs when the us dollar went to shit

items.title: THE LONG INJURY
items.why: A struck-down man's real card: his one pain line, his real days left, what he cannot do, all pulled from the real wiki numbers. You see it in the VOTE tab, item THE LONG INJURY.

items.title: THE BAR'S GLASS
items.why: A glass set down on the bar counter had no sound, and now it rings once, clear and short, like real glass. You hear it in the VOTE tab on its own page.

items.title: A DEATH SHOULD COST THE LIVING WORK. AND I FIXED A BUG OF MINE.
items.why: Nobody buries anybody in the game yet, and debts no longer pass to heirs, matching your ruling that debts die. You see it in the VOTE tab, where the heir's first day carries the body, the creditor, the house and the name.

show.src: FIXED: a dead man's debt does not pass to his heir (you rule: you inherit the person, not the bill). Assets, level, perks and gear still do.\nPROPOSED FIRST DAY OF AN HEIR: 1. carry him to the wall (you build, not dig, in this ground). 2. a creditor at the door: forgive, pay half, or take the house. 3. who is still in the house. 4. the name, said once.

items.title: MODS TO COPY
items.why: Seven whole example mods, from adding an enemy to changing a wage or a helmet, each with its patch, its one lesson and what the checker said. You see it in the VOTE tab when you tap one; the game does not load a mods folder yet.

items.title: WHEN A MAN WALKS
items.why: In Battle Brothers each unpaid day drops a man one mood step and only an angry man deserts, so a content hire walks on day 3, your 'couple of days'. You see it in the VOTE tab when you slide the days unpaid and change his nature.

items.title: AN ACT IS ONE FELT YEAR: 130 DAYS, FOUR SEASONS, ABOUT 30 NAMED MOMENTS.
items.why: The plan said a season per act, but the game has no seasons, so each act gets four seasons and about 30 named moments, with four reports telling the 35 years between acts. You see it in the VOTE tab, on this card.

show.src: FOUND: the game has no season or calendar, and keeps only 30 nights of history.\nPROPOSED: 130 days an act in four seasons of about 32 days. About one memorable event in every four days, each named in the feed.\nThe 35 years between acts are told by four reports: what the valley looks like, who is left, what the valley says of you, what you left standing.

items.title: THE STASH: SIX SUPPLIES AND HOW MANY DAYS EACH LASTS
items.why: Each of the six shows its count and what it buys you, so 50 food for four men on desert is 4 days, 2 hurt men burn 2 meds a day, and 30 rounds are 15 shots, with the wage due at noon and what the next town sells. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK; in the demo it opens when you tap the six in the top bar, once RUN wires it.

items.title: WHEN A SETTLEMENT COMES FOR YOU
items.why: Wrong a faction twice and its patrols hunt you and its caravans open to raiding, then it cools off by itself, using the two thresholds Battle Brothers states. You see it in the VOTE tab: one faction through two bad contracts and then the quiet mornings after.

items.title: WHEN THE DATA CHANGES
items.why: In eight days the data folder changed 44 times and only once could it break a mod, and four lines of policy, a version number, a written-for tag, a break note and a made changelog, keep it that way. You see it in the VOTE tab, on this card.

items.title: THE ROAD ITSELF CHARGES, THE TWIST HAS ONE REAL PRICE
items.why: Battle Brothers never prices distance, it just rolls more trouble on a longer road; one job states its own twist price in writing (lose some mules, lose half the pay). You see it in the records, not drawn yet, feeding TUNING and the settlement screen.

Seen in: not drawn yet, feeds TUNING and the settlement screen.

items.title: THE DEMO AGAIN: 2 FIXED, 18 STILL WRONG
items.why: Since the last check your men open at full size and stay on screen, and contracts show on the phone; places still never open and the fight still never says if you won. You see it in the demo, last round beside this round, screen by screen.

items.title: A RAID ON YOUR BASE
items.why: Once you build at your base, a crew comes for it: your phone tells you it is coming, if you are home you fight it at your gate on what you built, and if you stay away for four days they take the base. You see it on the map and the phone, then in the fight at your gate.

items.title: A BLOCK IS TWO THINGS TOUCHING
items.why: A parry was a dull filtered thud, and now it is a blade's edge catching a shield's wood-and-metal rim with a real bright click. You hear it in the VOTE tab on its own page.

items.title: THE MARKET AGAINST THE WIKI
items.why: The shop sells back at one seventh like Battle Brothers, but still ignores town size, your standing and 32 situations like a siege or a fair. You see it in the VOTE tab, at the bottom of the prices page.

items.title: A POLICE STATION FULL OF HOSPITAL WARDS
items.why: The same police station drawn twice: same walls, same doors, same rooms, because both are the game's own floor plan maker given the same building. The one on the right is what the game actually builds today, and fifteen of its nineteen rooms are hospital wards, because the table that picks the rooms exists in two places and the copies disagree, and you see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, NOT IN A TAB YET on a play surface.

items.title: THE FIGHT'S GROUND, SHARP
items.why: Close in, the fight's ground is now drawn straight from the original art, one art pixel on one screen pixel of the phone, where before it was shrunk to a third and blown back up; a tile keeps all its edges (106 percent of the file, it kept 32), and it still runs at 60 frames by day and by night. Open any fight and you see it in the asphalt, the cars and the lamps, in the VOTE tab and the demo, NOT IN A TAB YET.

items.title: THE THREE BODIES
items.why: Your face already runs in the family through the three generations, so I built the same thing for the body, one ancestor's shape pulling at his son and grandson by the same pull your face uses. You see it here, three men in the same clothes with three different builds, not three strangers.

items.title: WHEN THE PHONE TURNS
items.why: When you turn your phone sideways, the in-game phone used to run off the bottom of the screen under the speed buttons; now it moves to the left side and fits, the speed buttons keep the bottom right, and nothing covers anything. You see it on the map when you hold your phone sideways.

items.title: HOW FAR EACH WEAPON REACHES
items.why: Every weapon's reach against your rule that melee hits at 1 and every gun starts at 2: melee all pass, but a bow can only hit at exactly 7 tiles and our rifle at exactly 6, because the data copied each weapon's farthest reach into its nearest. You see it in the VOTE tab as one chart, with the pistol at 1 because it is a dagger underneath.

items.title: HOW BIG THE BOARD IS
items.why: Battle Brothers never says how big its map is, so every size we use is ours, and a 2 against 2 fight cuts a 32 tile board while the middle size is never picked at all. You see it in the VOTE tab when you slide your party and theirs and watch the board the fight cuts.

items.title: WHAT EACH ORIGIN STARTS KNOWN FOR
items.why: Every starting story begins with some fame, a good or bad name and a standing with the nearest powers, three begin hated, and our data has none of it yet. You see it in the VOTE tab, all fifteen listed.

items.title: WHAT THE STARTING KIT COSTS
items.why: Only one of the fifteen starting stories lists its gear, and priced in batteries it makes the Deserters the richest start of all though they are only labelled Medium. You see it in the VOTE tab, the kit and its price.

items.title: WHAT A STARTING COMPANY IS WORTH
items.why: The fifteen starting stories ranked by money plus what their men cost to hire: the hard ones start richer than the easy ones, so their difficulty is a rule, like losing when one man dies, and no money dial can change it. You see it in the VOTE tab as one ranked list.

items.title: DOES THE MONEY MATCH THE LABEL
items.why: Each of the fifteen starting stories is labelled Easy, Medium or Hard, and the hard ones are not the poor ones; they are hard because of a rule, like losing if one man dies. You see it in the VOTE tab as the starting money per man for each one.

items.title: PATCH INSIDE A LIST
items.why: For whoever makes mods: a mod can now change one entry in a list by name or position, or add and remove words, without copying the whole list. You see it in the VOTE tab on this item's page, with two example mods.

items.title: WHO GUARDS THE SIX PLACES
items.why: Each of the six legendary places is guarded by whoever holds its ground, sized by how hard the place is. You see it in the VOTE tab: six cards with the guard and what it is made of.

items.title: THE ROSTER SHOWS THE HURT: A MAN'S CARD BEFORE AND AFTER HE IS STRUCK DOWN
items.why: A man struck down in a fight leaves the line for LAID UP, and his card counts down his 30 to 40 days, names the injury he keeps for good, says it in one pain line and prices the clinic, and dragging him back into the line is refused. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, before on the left and after on the right.

items.title: THE TWIN: OUR GROUND AGAINST THE PACK YOU BOUGHT
items.why: You were right: our road, props and fight board beside your approved pack tiles at the same size, and the pack has 100 times the colour, real cracks, dark outlines and painted objects where ours has flat stamps. You see it in the fight's ground, ours on the left, your pack on the right.

items.title: WHAT THE KEEPER SEES
items.why: A loaf already costs one battery at the floor, so stealing one just skips paying it; the real question was getting caught, and a market stall is not a supermarket, so the keeper should usually see you. You see it in the records, not drawn yet, feeding TUNING and the stall interaction.

records/BOHEMIA_ECONOMY_DAY_64_THE_PRICE_OF_BREAD_AND_THEFT_10_10_26.md; banks/BOHEMIA_ECONOMY_TEST_LINES_9_5_26.md round 64.

Seen in: not drawn yet, feeds TUNING and the stall interaction.

items.title: EVERY FIGHT BOARD'S EDGES NOW JOIN
items.why: The cul-de-sac, the landfill and the lake shore were the last boards whose blocks did not line up; now all nine fight boards join with zero broken edges. Thumbs up and this is how every board is laid, and you see it in the COMBAT tab on those three boards.

diffs: EVERY PIXEL: these three boards are our cooked ground (flat fills, 18 to 29 colours per 96 px); his street tile has 2,400 to 4,600. This is why the family is a placeholder and not added to (rule 101).
SEAMS: his tiles meet by texture and never line up exactly; ours were forced to match by a copied 12-px ring, which the no-borders vote now forbids.
SCALE: the picture is the whole boards shrunk to fit, not 1:1; the 10/16 candidate (combat2-three-boards-from-the-whole-bank-10-16) is the one shown at 1:1.

items.note: COMBAT TWO 10/16: twin added for the gate (PLUMBER's 10/10 note); the picture is from before rule 89 and stays as it was; the boards it shows are placeholders of the cooked family (rule 101a).

items.title: THE KEEPERS
items.why: Six real crafts that fight with an animal, war dogs to camel cavalry, and the shape a company would need to carry one as a companion. You see it in the VOTE tab, item THE KEEPERS.

items.title: THE FLIP NOW OPENS AT THE FIRST CRISIS, NOT BEFORE.
items.why: As you ruled, nothing flips until the first crisis starts, around day 80 to 100. Read the card in the VOTE tab: a fresh game has no flip until the crisis clock calls it, and taking a base no longer opens act 2.

show.src:
Before the first crisis: one face on the phone, no flip.
The first crisis starts (day 80 to 100): act 2 opens and the game says which day.
Taking a base no longer opens act 2. A base taken in act 2 opens act 3.
The crisis clock and the opening card are not built yet, so today the flip stays dark.

items.title: THE FLIPPED PHONE: NOTHING ON YOUR MEN
items.why: With the phone on its side, the tip no longer sits over your men's legs, it moves up into the empty strip beside the faces, and the tape behind the faces now ends at the last face instead of smearing across the whole street. Turn your phone sideways in any fight and you see it, in the VOTE tab and the demo, NOT IN A TAB YET.

items.title: A COYOTE IS NOT A PHOTOGRAPH OF ITSELF ANYMORE
items.why: A coyote on the street used to be its own smaller, blurrier size and never moved a leg; this is a rig fix, not a new look, so no pixel changed and no reference twin exists for an animal nobody has downloaded art of. You see it here, three coyotes forced on screen so you do not have to go find one.

show.src:
records/BOHEMIA_THE_WILDLIFE_RIG_10_10_26.txt; a screenshot sits at slices/vote/CHARACTER_WILDLIFE_RIG.png and the page that frames it at slices/vote/CHARACTER_WILDLIFE_RIG.html, neither is an art sheet under rule 82 (zero new pixels, the coyote bank is untouched) and wildlife is not one of rule 82's named families, so no reference twin was invented.

Seen in: the record and the two files above; no tab yet, this is a rendering mechanism, not a look.

items.title: THE DEMO LOADS IN 22 SECONDS ON A PHONE, NOT 75
items.why: The demo was drawing a street, three workshop boards and the whole page twice before you could press BEGIN; now it skips them, so on a phone the start screen shows in about a second and BEGIN lights at about 22 s instead of 75. You see it when the DEMO first opens: the bar on top is before, the one below is now.

items.title: A CHILD OF ACT ONE CARRIES THREE HABITS: HOARDS, SLEEPS LIGHT, TRUSTS NO PAPER.
items.why: Right now an heir carries nothing from the era he grew up in. Read the card in the VOTE tab: three habits taken from real collapse research, each a refusal or a reflex and never a number.

show.src:
FOUND: an heir's traits come only from the parent. The anarchy decade leaves no mark on anyone.
REAL RESEARCH: people raised through collapse stay cautious with money, hoard food, sleep light, and distrust paper.
PROPOSED HABITS FOR ACT ONE'S CHILD: HOARDS (never sells the last of a thing). SLEEPS LIGHT (always reads the stranger first). TRUSTS NO PAPER (no IOUs, only goods and batteries).
Habits cost options, they are not bonuses.

items.title: THE HOUSES AT WAR
items.why: The factions are at war with each other, not only with you: enemies who meet on a road clash, and a base the world takes is Conquered, not burned, using the game's own canon and Battle Brothers' own numbers. You see it in the VOTE tab: who hates whom and one real day of them meeting.

items.title: THE WELL IS THE ONE THAT TAKES LONGER
items.why: Every lot already costs one battery and never pays itself back on purpose; what was still flat was the days to build, and a dug well is a real multi-day job next to a water tank's one. You see it in the records, not drawn yet, feeding TUNING.

items.title: EVERYTHING YOU OWN, IN ONE SCROLL, FOR THE FIRST TIME
items.why: A chat can only use what it can see, and two rounds ago a shopping card was about to ask you to buy wrecked cars and guns you already owned because they sat in a file nobody had opened, so every pack you have ever bought is now indexed: 294 packs, 8,674 tiles, sorted into nine families, each with a picture and a count, and the 1,927 you approved marked inside it instead of standing in for the whole thing. You see it in the VOTE tab, one tile out of each family at full size with the count beside it, and the number that should decide the next few rounds: 6,747 of your tiles have never been judged by anybody.

diffs: WHAT IS HIS: all of it. 294 packs and 8,674 tiles read straight out of the repo chunks, 294 contact pictures, nothing redrawn and not one pixel cooked.

WHAT CHANGED: the seven families the approved bank already decided are COPIED exactly for its 84 packs, never re-decided, so the index cannot contradict the bar; three more families the packs plainly hold are named for the first time (weapon 73 tiles, animal 13, and the cars stay under prop because July put them there).

WHAT IS STILL MISSING AND WAS NOT INVENTED: no licence, seller or receipt is recorded anywhere in the repo for any of the 294 packs. Every entry says 'not recorded' instead of carrying one this lane made up.

Walk a man past an enemy gunman in any fight and you see it, in the VOTE tab and the demo, NOT IN A TAB YET.

items.title: THE PARTS ROAD, ROUND TWO: THREE GUNS AND TWO LAMP POSTS BESIDE YOUR OWN, WITH YOUR OWN GRAIN IN THEM
items.why: Round one's no-drawing road had one gap (a flat shape carries five colours where your tile carries fifteen hundred), so this round fills every part with a patch cut from your own tile instead of a flat colour, your pixels land back one-to-one inside my shapes, and nothing is drawn. You see it in the VOTE tab: a pistol, a revolver, an SMG and two lamp posts, each beside your own at the same size, the old flat road and the new material road side by side, and the number that decided round one: the top eight colours carried 100 percent of the flat one and carry 24 to 46 percent of the material one, against 4 to 15 on yours.

diffs: WHAT IT FIXES: the grain. Every part is filled with a patch cut from the twin itself (16 by 16 where his surface has room), tiled on the pixel grid and shrunk by exactly four so his pixels land at 1:1; the pistol goes from 9 colours to 752 and its top eight from 100% to 24% (his 2,796 and 14%), and a set test proves every colour on it is one of his: zero that are not, on all five.

WHAT IT STILL DOES NOT FIX: the form. A trigger guard is a curve on every gun he owns and the law forbids one, so mine is a square U; his finial is a ball and mine is a square. The 2x strip on the card shows the shape composition for what it is.

WHAT IT IS FOR: things the packs do not have. These five are things he owns, because his own tile is the only honest score; the card asks whether the road stays on what he does not own (A), builds out the gun set the roster needs (B), or is dropped (C). Nothing is final before the moodboard.

items.title: A MAN STRUCK DOWN STAYS IN YOUR LINE AT ONE HIT POINT, HIS WOUND A PENALTY THAT FADES
items.why: After a bad fight your hurt men used to sit out a month and you were left fighting alone; now a man who goes down and lives stays in your line at one hit point, carrying his wound as a penalty that fades over its days and a mark for life, and the dead never come back. You see it in the DEMO on the crew screen (CREW) after any fight where a man goes down: before on the left, now on the right.

before_after.after: BUILD 10/26zc: all twelve in the line, each struck-down man's wound days on his face, his card's wound with a red arrow a stat, the clinic's after beside it

items.title: THE CLINIC SHOWS THE WOUND, THE DAYS AND WHAT IT CUTS, BEFORE YOU PAY
items.why: The town's clinic now shows each hurt man's wound with a red arrow for every stat it takes, the days left on a clock and the clinic's after beside it with both cut in half, then the price; paying halves the days and the penalty, and what he lost for life stays. You see it in the DEMO in any town with a clinic: tap the clinic after a fight where a man went down.

items.title: YOUR MEN WEAR THEIR WOUNDS: AN EYE PATCH, STAPLES IN THE SKULL, THE NOSE GONE, BLOOD AND A BAND-AID
items.why: When a man is struck down and lives, his face now shows it: a lost eye gets an eye patch, brain damage a stapled scar over a shaved line, a lost nose a hole in a ring of scar, a lost ear a raw stump, and a fresh wound dried blood and a band-aid that come off as he heals, each one built on his own 3D head and lit by the same sun as his face. You see it in the VOTE tab on you and your 11 starting men, all 18 marks at the portrait's size and the thumb's, and on the crew screen on any man who carries one.
options: A, the marks stay on their faces

before_after.before: his face today: the first column of every man's row (TODAY)
before_after.after: the same face wearing each mark, one mark a column, the mark's name under it

diffs: THE MARK FOR LIFE: ours puts a lost eye's patch, a lost nose's hole or a skull's staples on his own head for good; his face today shows nothing he has been through.

THE FRESH WOUND: ours adds dried blood run from a cut over the brow and a band-aid over it the day he is struck down, the blood gone past half his days and the band-aid gone when he heals; his face today never changes.
THE WHOLE COMPANY: ours is made for you and all 152 people who can join you, every mark at 128 and the 64 thumb; today only the plain face exists.

items.title: EVERY FACE BREATHES: YOUR CREW BLINKS, GLANCES AND WINCES WHEN HURT
items.why: Every face on screen now breathes about 15 times a minute on the game's beat, blinks every 3 to 6 seconds and glances to the side now and then, and a hurt man winces with his breath catching, every 5 seconds while the wound is fresh and less as it heals, all from renders of his own 3D face. You see it moving in the VOTE tab, his face today beside the same face breathing on you and three of your men, and live on the crew screen, the town and the spoils on every face.

before_after.before: his face today, still (the left of each pair)
before_after.after: the same face as every screen now draws it, breathing, blinking and wincing on the beat (the right of each pair), recorded off the real face painter

diffs: IT BREATHES: ours rises a pixel and settles every eight beats of the game's 120 (15 breaths a minute); his face today holds dead still.
THE EYES: ours blinks every 3 to 6 seconds and glances left or right now and then, his own eyelids and eyeballs rendered; his face today never blinks.
THE HURT: ours winces with the breath catching when he carries a wound, every 5 seconds fresh and every 14 for a mark for life; his face today looks the same hurt or whole.

items.title: THE CITY YOU HAVE NOT WALKED IS GREY TAPE, NOT BLACK: YOU SEE ITS SHAPE, NOT WHO IS THERE. YOUR OWN PINS. THE BOSS FOUND BY A SIGN, AND HIS PART OF TOWN CHANGES WHEN HE FALLS
items.why: Where you have not been is the city in grey under tape snow, not black, colour where you walk, and a held finger pins CAMP, DANGER, LOOT, SHOP or a word; a flyer near you marks THE POT, and when he falls his block gets its lights back and THE KITCHEN. items.title: EVERY HELMET AND BODY ARMOUR IS DRAWN ON THE MAN WHO WEARS IT: THE POLICE RIOT HELMET AND THE POLICE VEST FIRST, SEVENTEEN PLACEHOLDERS IN ALL

You see it in the fight, on the crew screen, at camp and on the map, and on this sheet: him bare, then wearing each one in all eight turns and in his portrait.

items.title: A TOWN IS SAFE: PRESS HEAL IN A TOWN AND THE HOURS PASS THERE; NOBODY CAN ATTACK YOU THERE OR RIGHT OUTSIDE
items.why: You could not rest in a town; the heal button did nothing there. Now HEAL in any town passes the hours right there at camp speed while the town goes on around you, and no crew can reach you inside or on the spot your LEAVE puts you, until you take a step. Press HEAL right after leaving, without moving, and you rest in that town instead of out on the street. You see it on the RUN tab: walk into a town hurt and press the phone's HEAL.
